notes.title: Dev Blog #26 - Supervolcano Update!
notes.content:
Welcome back to our Dev Blog!

We're excited to share our progress on our next major content addition: the Supervolcanic Eruption disaster!
[h1]A Cataclysmic Event[/h1]
Our upcoming update introduces the first supervolcanic eruption in modern human history. Coinciding with our Japanese translations, the event centers on the Kikai Caldera in Japan. Players will face:

[list]
[*] Tsunamis affecting coastlines across Asia
[*] Widespread respiratory issues caused by ash
[*] A mini ice age altering global climate
[*] Worldwide power shortages and food scarcity[/list]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43341328/c3c9eae03c30af7ae49479e86d6d1c403cbe29f3.png[/img]

We've based this disaster on historical events like the [url=https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Youngest_Toba_eruption]Toba supereruption[/url] 74,000 years ago and the 1815 [url=https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1815_eruption_of_Mount_Tambora]Mount Tambora eruption[/url], which resulted in the [url=https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Year_Without_a_Summer]Year Without a Summer[/url]. Our goal is to combine humanity’s known struggles when suffering large volcanic eruptions in the past, with the added complexities introduced by modern technology.
[h1]First Look[/h1]
We're thrilled to give you a sneak peek at the Volcano disaster's visuals:

[previewyoutube=Vzwd468YjW4;full][/previewyoutube]
[h1]Special Announcement[/h1]
We're also excited to reveal that our long-time streaming partner and friend, UserFriendsly, will be showcasing his hidden talent as a voice actor in our new Positive News videos! Let us know if you’re excited to hear him inside the game too!

Recently, he even got to lay his hands on the new disaster in an exclusive sneak peak, so go check out his stream if you're interested!

[url=https://www.twitch.tv/videos/2275756476?t=02h46m20s][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43341328/e0fe10f7a88875aad25e2ad541dbb7e92a3a4dda.png[/img][/url]

Click the image above for the Supervolcanic Eruption sneak peak stream!

——————————

That’s it for today. Join [url=https://discord.com/invite/CJevhYUhWT]our Discord community[/url] to watch streams, get the latest updates, participate in playtests, and connect with other players. We're always here to answer your questions!

notes.title: Dev Blog #25 - Updated roadmap!
notes.content:
Welcome back to our Dev Blog!

We have great news about our upcoming updates. Get ready for new languages, a hardcore mode, and fresh content!

[h1]Update 1.6: Language Support and New Features[/h1]

Language Expansion:

We're introducing support for German, Spanish, Brazilian Portuguese, and Russian. While these translations are still in the experimental phase, they allow us to reach a broader audience eager to play Project Planet in their native languages. We welcome your feedback on the translations through our Discord or Steam Community page!

New Features:
[olist]
[*] Hurricane Quickgame: Experience the last remaining quickgame version of an existing disaster. This mode features the Landfall and Flooding stages.
[*] Hardcore Mode: For players seeking an extra challenge, we're introducing a mode where score effects of your decisions are hidden. This will require you to carefully consider the potential consequences of your actions before committing to them.[/olist] [img]https://clan.akamai.steamstatic.com/images/43341328/332427e09c807f377b25d8ce5105bbde5c1a2ab0.png[/img]

With all disasters now available in quickgame variants, we're taking the next leap in content expansion. Update 1.7 will introduce an entirely new disaster: the Supervolcanic Eruption.

Early development is already underway, and we look forward to sharing more details as we approach the release. In this catastrophic scenario, humanity will face one of the largest volcanic eruptions in history. Players will need to manage:
[olist]
[*] The devastating impact on the immediate surroundings
[*] Large-scale tsunamis
[*] A global haze triggering a massive ice age[/olist]Stay tuned for more information on this epic new challenge coming to Project Planet!

[img]https://clan.akamai.steamstatic.com/images/43341328/834ce23fce21d4a674c68e1ffca93d612ad72f1f.png[/img]

notes.title: Dev Blog #23 - Update 1.4 & new demo!
notes.content:
Welcome back for another Dev Blog!

We are incredibly happy with the reception of Update 1.3 and the subsequent hotfix build, as well as the tremendous support we’ve received from our new player base in Asia! But we’ve been hard at work in the meanwhile, so let’s talk about the upcoming Update 1.4!

[h1]Connection Issues[/h1]
Before we talk about Update 1.4, we want to stress that we are aware of connection issues affecting the gameplay for Chinese players. We are currently working on a solution that we believe will solve this issue, but in the meanwhile players are recommended to use the free game accelerator we talked about earlier [url=https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/2224610/view/4192362393707209234](more info here)[/url] to mitigate the issue.

[img]https://clan.akamai.steamstatic.com/images/43341328/3b5d16c22615a1098ab83ac7e7b1d64ebd5f7bd9.png[/img]

[h1]Update 1.4[/h1]
The next big update brings a mix of fresh content, highly requested features and quality of life improvements, along with bug fixes.

First up, we're expanding the game’s content by introducing the Locust Plague quick game mode alongside the Virus and Solar Flare modes introduced in the last update.

[img]https://clan.akamai.steamstatic.com/images/43341328/3cbeee3272853c333f2ed9678301391b8dc67fcf.png[/img]

To ensure clarity and prevent any confusion, AI players now come with their own unique names and an unmistakable AI icon. No more shenanigans with players trying to confuse others by naming themselves “A.I.” (very clever though :P). Alongside this, we've given the cursor a makeover, adopting a Project Planet-inspired design that dynamically highlights clickable elements, making navigation a breeze.

Lastly, in response to requests from Twitch streamers, we've added an option to hide the lobby code on startup and for our Chinese players, we're enhancing their experience with a Chinese version of the tutorial video and Chinese voiceovers for the News Item.

[h1]Balance Improvements[/h1]
Moreover, Update 1.4 brings with it the most comprehensive set of balance improvements to date! With the influx of Chinese players, we've gathered a substantial amount of data on game balance. This update represents a significant step forward in refining and fine-tuning the balance, making the gaming experience even better for all players!

[img]https://clan.akamai.steamstatic.com/images/43341328/0f590170711c77bb016df4fe6c7a273dc30bece0.png[/img]

[h1]New Demo[/h1]
Lastly, we're excited to reveal that alongside Update 1.4, we'll be launching a brand new demo version of Project Planet! During development, keeping the demo up to date became quite a task, and we felt it didn't truly capture the game's quality. However, with the improvements in Update 1.4, we're confident that the game is now at a stage where we can maintain the demo effectively and re-release it for everyone to enjoy!

[img]https://clan.akamai.steamstatic.com/images/43341328/e8f70b9b876b267bf4fc66acebd068c93f45f3c4.png[/img]

——————————

That’s it for today. Keep an eye out for the many streams by [url=https://discord.com/invite/CJevhYUhWT]joining our Discord community[/url]. Here you can also stay up to date on the latest updates, find others to play with, join our playtests or get in touch and ask us questions!

notes.title: Project Planet is now live in China!
notes.content:
Today we have a very special announcement!

We have already given some clues in recent months, but after lots of preparation and very hard work together with our local publisher and partner GamerSky Games, we are finally ready to release Project Planet in China!

[h1]China release[/h1]
In China, we're thrilled to announce the launch of Project Planet under the name 我不背锅 (I Won’t Take The Blame), catering to both Traditional and Simplified Chinese-speaking players. This marks a significant milestone for us as we expand our reach into one of the largest gaming markets in the world.
[img]https://clan.cloudflare.steamstatic.com/images/43341328/dfc05422f55a3635910188fe89e745de55298eaa.png[/img]

[h1]Update 1.3[/h1]
China has a massive and passionate gaming community, and we couldn't be more excited to introduce our game to this whole new audience. We look forward to welcoming new players to the community and reading about their experiences with the game. Together with our partner GamerSky Games, we're dedicated to providing the best possible gaming experience for our Chinese players!
[img]https://clan.cloudflare.steamstatic.com/images/43341328/88b387e9c8b3b9feaf09d03dd608c242873bd343.png[/img]
In recent weeks, we already talked about all the features this new update will contain outside of Chinese translations, but check out [url=https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/2224610/view/5922868739493281291]the complete changelog here[/url] for the full list of changes!

[h1]Other Languages[/h1]
If you're not Chinese but eagerly anticipating the game in your own language, you might be curious about what this Chinese release entails for you. While it may require a bit more patience, the translation of the game into Chinese lays the groundwork for future language additions. notes.title: Update 1.2 is live!
notes.content:
We just released Update 1.2, our largest update so far!

This introduces the all-new Solar Flare disaster, as well as new turn and read time customization, notifications when someone used an ability on you, and lots of balance changes and bug fixing!

[previewyoutube=YQi2l0CaJHU;full][/previewyoutube]

Changes:
[list]
[*] Added the Solar Flare disaster to the game!
You can now play a large solar flare and coronal mass ejection, causing the destruction of satellites, energy grids and other ground technology. Humanity will be left without power, communication and eventually even food and water for months or even years.
[*] Added turn timers to the game.
You can now select how long players have to answer a question, ranging from 10 seconds to 3 minutes, or completely disabled. When the timer reaches 0, a random answer will be selected for the player. This should help keep the game moving along in case someone is AFK or not paying attention.
[*] Added Read Times to the game.
You can now customize the duration of notifications and news items to align with your reading speed. Opt for "Very Fast" settings to swiftly dismiss messages for an accelerated gaming experience.
[*] You will now receive a notification when you are targeted by another player’s ability. Tap the notification for more information, or dismiss it by pressing the X-button.
[*] Introduced a new option for Earth’s final decision in some stages, with a random (positive or negative) effect on Population at 0 Force cost.
[*] Reduced the length of the Virus disaster’s first stage by ~3 questions on average. This brings the disaster more in line with the other disasters’ lengths.
[*] Ability options now have titles. The tooltip explaining the effect (cooperative/hostile, self-interest or environmental) that was previously shown in the title is moved to just below the answer title.
[*] Added an overview of active and past Stages in the question screen on web.
[*] Made a wide range of improvements to existing texts.
[*] Changed the unlockable <33% Ecosystems and Pollution Incidents to -6 Population and -2 Ecosystems or Pollution, from -2 Population and -6 Ecosystems or Pollution. This change should create a bigger payoff for reaching the lowest threshold of Ecosystems and Pollution, as players tend to reach these levels towards the end of the game when the impact of Ecosystems and Pollution is lower.
[/list]
Balance changes:
[list]
[*] Decreased the impact of minus Population decisions by 3% to offset the previous change.
[*] Nerfed Earth and the Media’s impact on Population in Stage 3 and 4 of the Asteroid Impact, while increasing their impact on Ecosystems & Pollution. This should make it easier for Humanity to survive this disaster.
[*] Slightly nerfed Earth in the Hurricane disaster.
[*] Slightly nerfed World Leaders in the Asteroid Impact disaster, but buffed World Leaders in the Hurricane and Locust Plague disasters.
[*] Slightly nerfed Scientists in the Locust Plague disaster, but buffed Scientists in the Asteroid Impact disaster.
[*] Nerfed the Industry in the Virus disaster.
[*] Buffed the Public's endgame in the Virus and Asteroid Impact disasters.
[/list]
Bug fixes:
[list]
[*] Fixed an issue where an A.I. Earth could use more difficult Crises than human players.
[*] Fixed an issue where certain news items in Locust Plague stage 1 had incorrect titles and voiceovers.
[*] Fixed an issue where two decisions had no cost for a Scientists track in Asteroid Stage 1.
[*] Fixed two small issues with Earth Incident values.
[*] Fixed a blurry font in the settings menu.
[/list]

notes.content:
Welcome back for another Dev Blog!

Today we’ve got some exciting footage from the upcoming Solar Flare disaster, info on how you can help us playtest it, as well as Project Planet’s very first award!

[h1]Solar Flare Footage[/h1]
The Solar Flare starts with the detection of increased solar activity, where Scientists need to discover the flare’s potential impact on society and where its weak points lie. The rest of humanity needs to decide between spending their resources to prepare for the flare’s arrival or continuing business as usual for as long as possible.

[previewyoutube=b-JXn94pd2o;full][/previewyoutube]

The second Stage is all about the outburst hitting Earth, with beautiful auroras appearing all around the planet, power grids going offline and satellite destruction spiraling out of control. Players will be figuratively and literally in the dark until they manage to restore power and communication channels. A perfect opportunity to secretly prioritize your self-interests without other players finding out!

[previewyoutube=djkCRY4DRkU;full][/previewyoutube]

If these videos got you excited, you may want to join us for our first official playtest of the Solar Flare disaster. Turn timers give players a maximum amount of time to make decisions, ranging from 3 minutes (or completely disabled) all the way down to only ten seconds for a crazy speedrun.

The animation timers determine how long messages about decisions will stay on screen. Perfect for slow readers or those who prefer to skip every text with more than three words (are you even reading this?).

Last but not least, Project Planet has received its first official award! Back in June, we playtested our game at Game Taste’s Test & Play event in Rotterdam, which earned us a nomination for the “A Taste of Success” (best playtest) award. [img]https://clan.akamai.steamstatic.com/images/43341328/a0f3a93f504f0a290dad5e6b9f3e624479af85d6.jpg[/img]
[h1]Roadmap[/h1]
After update 1.1 we plan to implement the most-requested features by the community and continue adding more content. Please note that this roadmap is still subject to change, as we’re constantly gathering more feedback from players and reassessing our priorities accordingly.

[img]https://clan.akamai.steamstatic.com/images/43341328/e5832d218fedf7ca307a5bb03dbe77f3f2b10ed1.png[/img]
Clarifying these upcoming features and changes, we received lots of requests to add additional languages to the game. As our game contains over 200,000 words, it is simply too expensive for a small Indie studio like ours to translate the game in the traditional manner. To accommodate non-English speaking players however, we have set up a system using AI-translations to reach an acceptable quality. We then want to iteratively improve these translations over time, assisted by community members who have already offered their support with translations. More on this later!

The Solar Flare will be the next big disaster added to the game after the Asteroid. In this disaster, players will face a devastating coronal mass ejection, destroying energy grids, crashing satellites, and disrupting supply lines to plunge humanity into a new dark age.

Another much requested feature is the ability to adjust game speeds. To achieve this, we are (re)introducing customizable turn timers where players need to make a decision before the timer runs out. We are also giving players the option to adjust animation speeds, e.g. how long news items stay on-screen or how long Live Feed notifications stay centre screen before floating to the top right.

The new “Policy” feature will allow Humanity players to set certain policies to affect the planet’s Ecosystems and Pollution. This allows them to work against Earth more at the cost of their own Score, or improve their score at the expense of Humanity, as well as giving players a little more to do during other players’ turns.

Finally the Twitch integration will give streamers the option to let their chat take over the Public role. Viewers will be able to vote on options through polls, to decide whether they want to team up with the streamer and other players, or work against them. This feature was much-requested by streamers, so we hope this will add a whole new dynamic to streaming Project Planet!

——————————

That’s it for today. Keep an eye out for the many streams by [url=https://discord.com/invite/CJevhYUhWT]joining our Discord community[/url]. Here you can also stay up to date on the latest updates, find others to play with, or get in touch and ask us questions!

notes.title: Update 1.0.2 is live!
notes.content:
We just released update 1.0.2!

This update contains a new reconnect system for the master device, to prevent players from getting locked out of their game if the master device loses connection for a short amount of time, as well as a wide range of balance improvements and bug fixes.

Full changes:

Changes:
[list]
[*] Added a new reconnect system to the master device. This should prevent games from getting locked out of the game when the master device loses connection for a short period of time.
[*] Added the game version to the menu so players can see which build they’re playing on.
[*] Updated the Credits.
[/list]
Balance changes:
[list]
[*] Ability Self-Interest options now affect your target by 4 instead of 3, and reduce Population by 2. This should make them slightly less appealing.
[*] Ability Environmental options now affect your target by 4 instead of 3. This should make them slightly more impactful and appealing.
[*] Slightly buffed the Media role in the Locust Plague disaster and added an extra question at the end of Stage 4.
[*] Slightly nerfed the Public role in the Locust Plague disaster.
[*] Slightly nerfed the Industry role in the Virus and Hurricane disasters.
[/list]
Bug fixes:
[list]
[*] Fixed an issue where AI Earth would always select the Virus. Additionally, AI Earth will now choose different disasters when playing multiple games in a single game session.
[*] Fixed an issue that would cause the game to end early in Virus Stage 4.
[*] Fixed an issue where “investigation of decision makers” in Hurricane Stage 4 would negatively affect the Media instead.
[*] Fixed multiple issues with News Item voiceover volume levels.
[*] Fixed multiple spelling mistakes.
[*] Removed unnecessary “Funding received:” texts in certain research tracks.
[/list]

notes.title: Dev Blog #16 - First week of release!
notes.content:
Welcome back for another Dev Blog, the first one since Monday’s game launch!

Today we’re covering the amazing time we had in the first days of the release, changes coming in the first updates, and we’re revealing the final winners of the community meme contest.
[h1]Release[/h1]
Monday was a dream come true for us. With lots of people tuning in to Twitch to see the official release ([url=https://www.twitch.tv/videos/1934741606]VOD here[/url]) and going from Popular Upcoming Releases to New & Trending on Steam within a few hours, it far exceeded our expectations for our tiny indie game. Thanks so much for all your support!

[img]https://clan.cloudflare.steamstatic.com/images/43341328/4e442c21257ec5fa912d572400c7de9722e3e8ad.png[/img]
[h1]Next Updates[/h1]
While we’re trying our hardest to enjoy the moment with the great reception and all the new players finding out about Project Planet, it’s also time to look to the future. We already have two updates in development, one being a smaller update with mostly bug fixes and improvements, and one being a larger content update that will introduce the much anticipated Asteroid Impact disaster to the game!

The smaller update will be patch 1.0.2 and is expected to be released within the next week. Some of the changes included in this build are:
[list]
[*] A new reconnect system for the master device, to prevent players from getting locked out of their game if the master device loses connection for a short amount of time.
[*] A variety of balance changes.
[*] Fix for a bug that would cause an AI Earth to always select the Virus disaster.
[*] Multiple fixes to small bugs and game stoppers.[/list]
Next up is Update 1.1, the first large update that will introduce the Asteroid Impact disaster to the game, as well as a rework of the Crisis. This should make the Crisis less punishing for the Earth player if it’s unsuccessful.

If you want to help us test this new update, be sure to join our weekly community dev stream on Fridays, or join one of the many streamers that have received early access to this content. You can find these streams under Events tab and #livestreams channel [url=https://discord.com/invite/CJevhYUhWT]on the official Discord.[/url]

[previewyoutube=a9RENAeJ0pY;full][/previewyoutube]

We were also overwhelmed by all the great feedback and suggestions we received since the launch. We’re currently gathering a list of all the requests, and setting priorities to integrate these changes into the game. It greatly helps us determine what players want to see added or changed, so please keep ‘em coming!

A few examples of improvements or suggestions from players we are currently looking at:
[list]
[*] Game translation into other languages and subtitles
[*] Twitch integration (so Twitch chat can collectively influence the game)
[*] Mod support for players to create their own scenarios
[*] (Adjustable) turn and notification timers
[*] Skip function for news videos and items
[*] Borderless windowed mode
[*] And many more![/list]

Today we’re also announcing the final winners of the community meme contest!

A big congrats to Blue_Star, Raiking and Conradillac for taking home 1st, 2nd and 3rd place respectively! They will be awarded a free game key or be featured in-game in a custom news item, according to their choice. Congrats!

[img]https://clan.cloudflare.steamstatic.com/images/43341328/152d98ccf2e344007dcb9b0d5448d8ef4a0c465b.jpg[/img]

notes.title: Update 0.12 is live!
notes.content:
We just released update 0.12! This introduces lots of new and improved gameplay features, like a complete overhaul and clearer communication of how Ecosystems and Pollution allow Earth to unlock new questions and Incidents, as well as some balance tweaks and minor bug fixes.

Full changelog:

Changes:
[list]
[*] Players now receive a turn notification screen in the colour of their role on their mobile device to warn them when it’s their turn.
[*] Reintroduced the options button in the lobby. This time without game breaking bugs.
[*] You can now remove players from the Lobby and select a new party leader on the master device.
[*] Added Game Credits to the main menu
[*] Added two new unlockable Incidents to Planet Earth.
[*] Earth’s unlockable Incidents are now unlocked at 67% and 33% Ecosystems and Pollution, instead of only at 50%.
[*] Earth’s Incidents that are only available when Ecosystems or Pollution is under 66% or 33% will now be available immediately after meeting this condition, instead of only after Earth used another Incident. (Senzi, you’re welcome)
[*] Unlocked questions and Incidents now show the unlock criteria, and a red outline and fill colour to more clearly differentiate them from regular questions and Incidents.
[*] Updated the Ecosystems and Pollution’s score bars on the master device, to more clearly communicate the unlock criteria for unlockable questions and Incidents.
[*] Replaced the role names with player names in the Stage Results and Game Over screen, to make it clearer which player won (role icon still shows which role won).
[*] Earth’s Influence Scores question at the end of each stage now has a different background image to make it stand out.
[*] The Game Over screen now has separate SFXs and music depending on whether Earth or Humanity won.
[*] Improved the names and wording for Nemesis, Stage Results, Crisis Results and Game Over awards.
[*] Earth now has a unique Nemesis screen, showing which player had the most positive and negative impact on the Population, Ecosystems and Pollution (combined).
[/list]

Balance changes:
[list]
[*] Slightly nerfed Public and Industry in Hurricane disaster, while buffing Media and Earth.
[*] Slightly nerfed Earth in Virus disaster.
[*] Slightly buffed World Leaders and Media in Locust Plague disaster.
[/list]

Bug fixes:
[list]
[*] Fixed an issue where Earth wouldn’t always have three Incident options to choose from. (again welcome, Senzi)
[*] Fixed an issue where the music would stop playing when a News Video would bring the Population below or above a threshold where another song starts playing.
[*] Fixed an issue where the Earth Influence choices in the first tab of the Results Screen would show outdated icons for -8 Population, Ecosystems or Pollution.
[*] Fixed an issue where the Crisis could trigger in the background of a News Video.
[*] Fixed an issue where “Power” was called “Influence” in the Power tutorial popup.
[*] Fixed multiple incorrect News Item voiceovers.
[*] The Crisis timer on the master device and mobile devices are now more in-sync.
[*] Many minor fixes to texts and scores.
[/list]

notes.title: Update 0.10 is live!
notes.content:
We just released update 0.10.1, addressing a large list of issues and points of feedback from Steam Next Fest and our Discord community!

This update fixes the issue where abilities wouldn't always work when used, increases turn timers of the AI to make it easier to follow what's going on, and fixes an issue where the game wouldn't always end when the population hit 0, among many other things.

For a full list, check the change log below:

Changes:
[list]
[*] Increased AI decision timers by 3s and another 0.5s for each additional AI in the game (after one). This should make it easier to follow what’s going on for new players, especially when playing singleplayer.
[*] Decreased impact of Population effects by ~5%.
[*] When players bid the same amount in a Crisis where Humanity spent enough resources, the ability will now go to the player with the most Power instead of the player who was fastest to answer.
[*] Reduced Force cost of cheapest Trigger Incidents (-2 Ecosystems/Pollution) for Planet Earth from 2 to 1.
[*] Adjusted certain Trigger Incident values that made these options too unappealing.
[*] Reduced the impact of Earth’s "Heart Failure" option in Virus Stage 4 from -6 to -4 Population, to reduce the extreme Population decline at the end of the stage.
[*] Earth decisions that cost 0 Force will now also show the Force cost behind the titles.
[*] Added disaster-specific background images to the web environment.
[/list]

Bug fixes:
[list]
[*] Fixed an issue where abilities would not always activate when used on the same target more than once.
[*] Fixed an issue where the Population would count down to 0 and then suddenly jump back to a previous value, not ending the game.
[*] Fixed an issue where the game would not end if the Population hit 0 during the Stage Results Screen.
[*] Fixed an issue where Notifications and the Live Feed would not show up in future games when players returned to lobby at a specific time.
[*] Fixed an issue that caused texture settings to always be set to Low by default.
[*] Fixed an issue where the wrong tag would be displayed on certain abilities.
[*] Fixed an issue where Population decline from Ecosystems & Pollution was swapped in the score screen.
[*] Fixed an issue where two options in the Industry abilities would have the swapped score effects.
[*] Fixed an issue where players that were disconnected when the Crisis started could not spend any points.
[*] Fixed an issue where the icon representing score being spent on the Crisis was blue (points gained) instead of red (points lost).
[*] Fixed a visual issue with the Research Completed banner on mobile.
[*] Fixed an issue where the Industry would not always get a question in Virus stage 1.
[*] Fixed an issue where the wrong news item would show in Virus stage 2.
[*] Fixed an incorrect Live Feed message in Virus stage 3.
[/list]

notes.title: Dev Blog #11 - Last week’s madness!
notes.content:
Welcome back for another Dev Blog!

Last week has been a hell of a ride, and by far the wildest week in Project Planet’s history with lots to talk about!
[h1]Steam Next Fest[/h1]
From the very first evening (Europe time), Next Fest has been one huge party. Throughout the week we quadrupled our wishlists and welcomed over fifty new players to [url=https://discord.com/invite/CJevhYUhWT]our Discord community[/url]. Thanks to Twitch streamers [url=https://twitch.tv/userfriendsly]UserFriendsly[/url] and [url=https://twitch.tv/coppersantv]Coppersan[/url], as well as [url=https://twitter.com/GameTastes]Game Taste[/url], we were able to set up live streams for every day of the week and see the game in action. We had a blast interacting with the players, gathering their feedback, meeting new people and seeing the Discord community come to live!

[img]https://clan.akamai.steamstatic.com/images/43341328/53df54a8bfe476e5228cdb79f1b60d542d693978.png[/img]
[h1]Lot’s of Streamers[/h1]
The highlight of our week was undoubtedly seeing lots of people try Project Planet on all these livestreams. During one of the streams we reached over 20,000 concurrent viewers (one of the top streams of the entire festival) and over 200,000 viewers joined in total. Incredible!

If you had fun participating in these streams, follow the #livestreams channel on our Discord as we plan to set up regular livestreams soon! In the meanwhile, here are some more amazing numbers from last week:

[img]https://clan.akamai.steamstatic.com/images/43341328/2478af9a4c508bbd0c373f1ad32e91352b614fa8.jpg[/img]
[h1]Indigo Festival[/h1]
On Wednesday we attended [url=https://indigoshowcase.nl/]Indigo Festival[/url] in Utrecht, The Netherlands, as one of the 22 selected showcases. Throughout the event, roughly a hundred industry professionals got to try out Project Planet and give feedback. We were totally overwhelmed by the amount of positive feedback and interest we received from our peers. More on this may be coming soon!

[img]https://clan.akamai.steamstatic.com/images/43341328/74eeabd6440f9179edcdd93949fdd711a3140e37.png[/img]
[h1]The Future[/h1]
Now with Next Fest and Indigo behind us, the logical question is… what’s next?

First of all, we are happy to announce our demo will stay available even now that Next Fest has ended, and will continue to be available at least until the full release in late Q3.

We will also be working with content creators to give players an exclusive sneak peek of the other Disasters coming with the full release (Asteroid Impact, Locust Plague & Hurricane), so make sure to keep an eye out for that on Discord.

At the same time, we will focus on fixing some of the biggest issues currently in the demo:
[list]
[*] Players sometimes won’t see their question until they refresh the browser.
[*] Sometimes abilities are lost without being used when activated.
[*] The game will not always end immediately when the Population reaches 0.
[/list]
And we’ll be looking at making more quality of life changes. Some of the possibilities being considered are:
[list]
[*] Giving Humanity players more to do when it’s not their turn.
[*] Giving Humanity players more impact on Ecosystems and Pollution.
[*] Allowing players to take control of a role played by AI when the game is already in progress.
[*] Adding Twitch stream integration and other support for content creators
[/list]
Last but not least, if you're excited about the full release, [b][u]you'd do us a HUGE favour if you could tell a friend about Project Planet[/u][/b]! Any extra wishlists we can get will go a long way in securing the funding and visibility that's necessary to make Project Planet the best it can be!

That’s it for today. Let us know which changes you’re looking forward to the most on [url=https://discord.com/invite/CJevhYUhWT]our Discord community[/url]! And be sure to wishlist Project Planet below.

notes.title: Update 0.9 is live!
notes.content:
We just released update 0.9.1 in preparation for Steam Next Fest that's starting on Monday.

This update introduces a new tutorial video for new player, kick options for the party leader to remove unwanted or disconnected players from the game, and lots of smaller fixes.

Changes:
[list]
[*] Added a Tutorial Video to the game, which the Party Leader can start while in the Lobby Screen.
[*] The Party Leader now has a kick function to remove unwanted or disconnected players from the game.
[*] Kicked players will now be taken over by AI for the remainder of the game, to prevent games from getting stuck when a player has to leave or is unable to rejoin.
[*] Replaced “-4 Population” with “all scores x1.25” in Earth’s final question of Virus Stage 1.
[*] Increased the length of Virus Vaccines Stage by approximately 4 questions.
[/list]
Bug fixes:
[list]
[*] Fixed an issue where World Leaders wouldn’t always get at least one question in Virus Vaccines Stage.
[*] Fixed an issue where some research tracks were unclear.
[*] Fixed an issue where “Funding received” for Scientists showed 0 when 4 funding was received.
[*] Fixed an issue where a news item voiceover was partially cut off.
[*] Fixed an issue where the answer types for Scientists' negative ability targeting World Leaders would occasionally be incorrect.
[*] Fixed an issue where the wrong News Item was sometimes shown in Virus Stage 2.
[*] Fixed an issue where the icon would indicate players would receive score instead of lose score when bidding on the Crisis (blue squares instead of red squares).
[/list]

notes.title: Announcing Project Planet - Earth vs Humanity!
notes.content:
We are extremely proud to announce Fifth Harbour Studio’s very first game; Project Planet!

Multiplayer couch games and complex board games have been increasingly popular over the last decade, and if the pandemic has taught us anything, it’s the importance of being able to have a good time with friends and family. Whether in person or online.

It has also renewed our awareness of the fragility and flaws of our exceptional civilization and the risks we face as a species. Project Planet perfectly captures these two developments in a unique blend of existing game genres and dramatic themes.

[previewyoutube=EdzLLFRId1E;full][/previewyoutube]

[h1]What is Project Planet?[/h1]

Project Planet is a 1v5 serious party game where you can cooperate with and against your friends. Impossible dilemmas with strong real-life parallels, and branching narratives create countless ways to survive cataclysmic disasters like virus outbreaks, solar flares and asteroid impacts. Or you can take control of the disasters as Planet Earth, and destroy humanity altogether!

Will you save your fellow humans, or destroy them?

[h1]What roles can I play?[/h1]

You can choose between Planet Earth and one of Humanity’s roles. As Earth, you will take on up to five of your friends. Your goal is to stop humanity from doing further harm, by wiping them off the planet.

Humanity is made up of five distinct roles – World Leaders, Industry, Scientists, Media, and the Public – each with its own gameplay style and the need to collaborate for survival. However, the goal is not just the survival of the human race, but also the pursuit of power and influence among players.

[h1]What is the gameplay like?[/h1]

Project Planet challenges players with complex dilemmas that require careful consideration of not only the immediate effects of their decisions but also their potential future consequences. The game's narrative drives the need to negotiate, cooperate, and strategically utilize abilities to align with those acting in the best interest of humanity and oppose those who are not.

And here's the best part; your friends don't even need to own the game to play with you! Even if they can’t come over to your house, all you need to do is use a video conference tool to stream the game to them, have them visit www.projectplanet.tv on their phone or PC, and their browser will become their controller. It's that easy!

*or any other web-enabled device

[h1]Why Early Access?[/h1]

We strive to make Project Planet the best it can be and recognize that the player base plays a crucial role in game development alongside our team. While we are launching with a wealth of content, we have much more planned. Your feedback during the first months of Early Access will be invaluable in refining game balance and addressing any issues you may encounter.

Whether you intend to save humanity or destroy it, we would love to get your input. Join our Discord to keep up to date on the development, and participate in our community to bring Project Planet to the next level!

Please follow us on our social channels for more updates here! More from us soon!
